originality.rationale: The 2026 source gives the process and occupation transform, but does not derive the positive-width landing probability, its exact rare-target coefficient, exponential limit, or clock-sum threshold. Resetting literature on Brownian paths or lattice targets is not an implication of the asserted continuous-jump landing law. Published indexed findings and the available earlier research claims were compared on objects, statements and stronger coverage; residual risk from unindexed general rare-set theorems is explicit.
residual_risks: A stronger unindexed small-target theorem for uniformly regenerating continuous-state chains could subsume the exponential-law portion; priority must be checked by domain experts.
The Phys. Rev. E 2015 and 2024 papers and the SIAM narrow-capture article were accessed at abstract level, not their full primary texts; no whole-document noncoverage claim is made.
Only the available earlier research claims and bounded indexed queries were examined, so a partition alone does not prove uniqueness.

value.rationale: Precise nonzero detector width is central to physically interpreting instantaneous jump searches. The exact inverse-density search-time coefficient, exponential capture-time scaling, and sharp Pareto clock-sum threshold distinguish landing from Brownian crossing and permit quantitative finite-width detector calibration in a model with individually infinite-mean competing clocks.
